minors.detail:
app.css:41 sets `--color-primary: oklch(85% 0.08 240)` for the dark theme — 85% lightness, 0.08 chroma. Rendered, "Choose files" is a soft pastel blue with near-black text, which reads more like a disabled or selected chip than a service-accent CTA; the mockup's is a saturated Material blue with white uppercase text. Meanwhile the light theme (app.css:24) uses `oklch(45% 0.19 265)` — a different hue family (indigo, 265) at more than double the chroma.

So the accent is both off the reference and inconsistent between the two themes the app can serve.
minors.fix: Pick one accent hue and derive both themes' primary from it (Navidrome's own Material blue), adjusting only lightness/contrast per theme. Check contrast of --color-primary-content against it in both.

minors.title: The iPad/iPhone subhead is not implemented
minors.detail: Section 1 ratifies two subheads: "add music to the library" on desktop and "add music" on iPad/iPhone. App.svelte's subhead switches only on `collectionMode`, so the long desktop string renders on every phone, where it is the copy most at risk of wrapping under the masthead at 320px.
minors.fix: Fold `isIOS` into the ternary: private keeps "your tags, its own section"; otherwise `isIOS ? 'add music' : 'add music to the library'`.

minors.title: The slow-connection downshift note never renders
minors.detail: Section 2 ratifies "Slow connection. Switching to smaller pieces so progress sticks." The store tracks the downshift (`downshiftedChunkBytes`, set from the tus driver's `onDownshift`) but no component reads it, so nothing in web/src ever prints that string. A contributor on a weak connection watches throughput drop with no explanation, which is the moment the note was written for.
minors.fix: Render the note in the uploading branch (next to WakeLockBar) whenever any current file has a non-null `downshiftedChunkBytes`.

minors.title: The Matched line prints empty parentheses when the match carries no year
minors.detail: `matchedLine` is gated on `matchedArtist` alone, then interpolates `(${outcome.matchedYear})` unconditionally. `matched_year` is `omitempty` on the wire and the store defaults it to '', so a match without a year renders "Matched: Artist - Album (). You can close this page now." in front of the family, at the flow's single moment of success.
minors.fix: Build the parenthetical conditionally: append ` (${year})` only when `matchedYear` is non-empty.

minors.title: A MusicBrainz outage is chipped "pushed back" in history, a verdict word for a non-verdict
minors.detail: `chipText` maps both 'pushed-back' and 'probe-unavailable' to "pushed back". The second state means the matching service never answered; the album is fine and waiting. The expanded disclosure says so honestly ("Can't check MusicBrainz right now"), but the collapsed row a user scans reads as a rejection they have to act on. Section 9's chip vocabulary has no entry for the state.
minors.fix: Give 'probe-unavailable' its own chip, "check again" (or "not checked yet"), and add it to section 9's list; it keeps `badge-warning` and the same disclosure behavior.

minors.title: Sizes render in MiB and GiB, engineering units in family-facing copy
minors.detail: formatBytes prints "2.0 GiB" and "512.0 MiB", and those strings fill section 1's `{max_album_size}` token and section 2's "{acked_bytes} confirmed / of {total_bytes}" readout. GiB is a unit a family reader does not use, and the forced one decimal makes the format-panel limit read "up to 2.0 GiB" where "up to 2 GB" is what a person would say. The comment justifies the choice by matching internal/serve's `humanGiB`, which is log output, not contributor copy.
minors.fix: Keep one implementation but render human units: GB/MB labels, and drop a trailing ".0" so the limit reads "2 GB" while a progress figure can still read "1.4 GB".

minors.title: The server's own sign-out and roster copy diverges from the ratified strings
minors.detail: Three small drifts on the Go side. `unauthenticatedFailure.Message` says "Your sign-in has expired. Reload the page to sign in again." while section 2 ratifies "Your sign-in expired. Reload to sign in again, then pick the upload back up from Your uploads." -- and the server string is user-visible, since a document request renders it through http.Error as a bare page. The warm roster page heads "You're not on the list yet" and then calls the same thing "the family list" in the next sentence. Its `<title>` is the bare product codename "dubplate" rather than the configured site name, as is App.svelte's masthead fallback at line 323.
minors.fix: Align the 401 message with section 2 verbatim, use "the family list" in both the warm page's heading and body, and feed Serve.SiteName into the warm page title and the masthead fallback so no surface ships the codename.

minors.title: Institutional register in the too-many-uploads explanation, and three unratified strings
minors.detail: ReasonTooManySessions's Friendly reads "You already have the maximum number of uploads in progress." -- "the maximum number of" is the institutional register the kind-copy calibration rules out; a person says "You have too many uploads going right now." Separately, three user-facing strings appear nowhere in the contract and were never ratified: History's "Untitled album" placeholder (History.svelte:108), the desktop "Choose a folder" button (App.svelte:392), and Journey's screen-reader-only "Adding it to the library now." (Journey.svelte:149) where the visible sublabel says "adding it now".
minors.fix: Reword the Friendly line and update the email golden. Add the three strings to the contract with a decision on each: "Untitled album" reads fine, "Choose a folder" needs a place in section 1's desktop list, and the announcement should match the sublabel it voices.

minors.title: Journey's announce effect writes $state it reads in the same effect, forcing a redundant re-run
minors.detail: `let lastAnnouncedJourneyState = $state<string | null>(null)` is read at line 170 and written at line 173 inside the same `$effect`. Svelte 5 schedules the effect to re-run on that write; the second pass takes the early return, so it converges rather than looping — but it is the exact self-referential-effect shape the docs warn about (https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/$effect#When-not-to-use-$effect), and it costs an extra effect pass per poll for no benefit. The value is never read from the template, so it does not need to be reactive at all.
minors.fix: Make it a plain `let lastAnnouncedJourneyState: string | null = null;` — an effect-internal memo, not component state. If it must stay `$state` for any reason, read it under `untrack(() => lastAnnouncedJourneyState)`.

minors.title: WakeLock: concurrent toggles leak a sentinel, and release() can reject out of onDestroy
minors.detail:
This is residue check (a). The rune usage itself is correct: `on = $state(false)` in a class inside a `.svelte.ts` file is the right shape, `supported` is correctly a non-reactive `readonly` capability probe, and passing one instance from App.svelte into both `WakeLockBar` and `Journey` is the right way to keep the toggle's state across the hand-off. Two behavioral defects, both untested:

1. `toggle()` awaits `nav.wakeLock.request('screen')` while `this.on` is still `false`. A second tap during that await passes the same `if (this.on)` check and issues a second request; whichever resolves first has its sentinel overwritten by the second at line 45 and is never released — a screen lock the user can no longer turn off from the UI.
2. `release()` (line 56) does not guard `await this.sentinel.release()`. `WakeLockSentinel.release()` rejects if the sentinel was already released (which the browser does on its own when the tab backgrounds). `sentinel` and `on` then keep stale values, and `Journey`'s `onDestroy(() => { void wakeLock.release(); })` (line 127) and `App.resetSelection`'s `void wakeLock.release()` (App.svelte:177) both turn that into an unhandled rejection at teardown.

Risk assessment for the missing test file: low blast radius (a wake lock is a nicety, and `supported` gating means it is absent entirely on Firefox/older Safari), but it is the one module in web/src with no test at all, and both defects above are trivially unit-testable against a fake `navigator.wakeLock`.
minors.fix: Add an in-flight guard (`private requesting = false;`, set around the await, early-return when set) and wrap the release in `try { await this.sentinel.release(); } catch { /* already released */ } finally { this.sentinel = null; this.on = false; }`. Add `web/src/lib/wakeLock.svelte.test.ts` with a stub `navigator.wakeLock` covering: unsupported (no request issued, `on` stays false), request → `on` true, browser-initiated `release` event → `on` false, double-toggle → exactly one sentinel, and a rejecting `release()` → `on` false and no throw.

minors.title: Hardcoded DOM ids in AlbumCard and CollectionPicker instead of $props.id()
minors.detail: `album-artist`, `album-title`, `album-year`, and `track-title-${index}` (AlbumCard.svelte:65-107) plus `collection-picker` (CollectionPicker.svelte:38) are literals. Only one instance of each mounts today, so nothing is broken — but any second instance produces duplicate ids, which silently breaks `<label for>` association and is exactly the class of bug that survives a refactor unnoticed. `$props.id()` (Svelte 5.20+; the repo is on 5.57) exists for this.
minors.fix: `const uid = $props.id();` then `id={`${uid}-artist`}` / `for={`${uid}-artist`}`, and `id={`${uid}-track-${index}`}` for the per-track rows. Same in CollectionPicker. See https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/$props#$props.id()

minors.title: pendingFiles and preflightRejections are deep $state proxies over values that are only ever replaced wholesale
minors.detail:
`pendingFiles = $state<File[]>([])` and `preflightRejections = $state<PreflightVerdict[]>([])` are both assigned only by wholesale replacement (App.svelte:119, 127, 172-173), never mutated element-wise. `$state` builds a deep proxy for them anyway. It happens to work — Svelte's `proxy()` leaves non-plain objects alone, so `File` instances pass through unproxied and `preflightVerdictsByFile.get(file)` (App.svelte:312-316) still matches on identity — but that correctness rests on an implementation detail of which prototypes Svelte proxies, in a Map keyed on `File` object identity. `$state.raw` is the documented rune for a value that is always replaced and never mutated (https://svelte.dev/docs/svelte/$state#$state.raw), and it removes the proxying question entirely.

By contrast `tagTrackTitles` (App.svelte:65) *is* mutated element-wise at line 438 and must stay a deep `$state`. `uploadStore.files` is likewise correctly deep — `startFile`'s callbacks mutate `entry.progressBytes` in place.
minors.fix: `let pendingFiles = $state.raw<File[]>([]);` and `let preflightRejections = $state.raw<PreflightVerdict[]>([]);`. No call-site changes are needed since both are only ever reassigned.

minors.title: The progress effect keeps running after all files land and can clobber Journey's outcome announcement
minors.detail:
The effect's guard is `phase !== 'uploading'`, which stays false once Journey mounts (Journey renders inside the `phase === 'uploading'` branch). Once every file is `ok`, `ackedBytes === size`, so the computed percentage is exactly 100 — and `shouldAnnounceProgress` returns `true` unconditionally at `percent >= 100` (announce.ts:24). Meanwhile `announceState` resets `lastPercent` to `null` (announce.ts:91), so any re-run of this effect after Journey has announced "Matched: …" or "No MusicBrainz match…" overwrites that outcome text in the shared region with "100 percent confirmed". In practice `currentFiles` stops changing after landing, so this needs a concurrent `uploadStore.files` mutation to fire — but the two writers share one region with no coordination.

Related, lower-value: `LiveRegion.write` sets `textContent` unconditionally, and an `aria-live` region does not re-announce identical text. Two consecutive `announceState('Waiting its turn.')` calls (already prevented by Journey's own memo) or an outcome that repeats a prior message would be silently dropped.
minors.fix: Extend the guard to `if (phase !== 'uploading' || allFilesLanded || currentFiles.length === 0) { return; }` so the progress voice hands off cleanly to Journey's state voice. Optionally give `LiveRegion.write` a no-op-breaking nudge (clear then set on a microtask) for the repeat-message case.

minors.title: uploadStore.files grows without bound across uploads in one page session
minors.detail: `addFile` pushes onto `files` and nothing ever removes an entry. `App.currentFiles` filters by `uploadFileIds` so the display stays correct, but every album uploaded in one page session leaves its rows (and their `File` objects, retained by the private `fileObjects` Map — the actual memory cost) behind permanently. `resetSelection` does not clear `uploadFileIds` either, so between a reset and the next `beginUpload` the derived `currentFiles` still resolves to the previous, all-`ok` selection, which is what makes `allFilesLanded` fragile.
minors.fix: Add a `clearFinishedFiles()` (or fold it into the `resetSession()` from the first finding) that drops entries whose status is `'ok'` and which carry no resume anchor, deleting their `fileObjects` entries, and have `App.resetSelection()` also set `uploadFileIds = []`.

minors.title: The page has no <h1>; the site name is a bare span
minors.detail: The masthead renders `<span class="text-xl font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide">`. The only headings in the document are the `<h2>` in History/SpecCard and the `<h3>`s in the alerts, so the heading outline starts at level 2 or 3 with no document title landmark. A screen-reader user navigating by heading has no top-level anchor, and the heading levels skip.
minors.fix: Make the masthead an `<h1 class="text-xl font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide">` (visual styling is unchanged since Tailwind classes carry the size), and keep the section headings at `<h2>`.

minors.title: App.svelte — the composition root holding the whole phase machine — has no test file
minors.detail: Every component and lib module has a `.test.ts` except App.svelte and wakeLock.svelte.ts. App.svelte owns the `Phase`/`View` state machine, the selection → preflight → tagging → upload routing, `journeySessionId`'s stale-session derivation, resume re-pick matching, and the progress live-region effect. All three of the reachability-critical findings above (stale session, blank page on config failure, no path back after success) are exactly the kind of cross-phase transition a component-level test can never catch, and none of them is caught by the 144 passing tests.
minors.fix: Add `web/src/App.test.ts` rendering App with an injected fake store, covering at minimum: config failure renders an error rather than nothing; a ZIP upload following a multi-file upload finishes the *new* session id; and resetSelection clears session state. This needs the store to be injectable into App (it is currently imported as the module singleton at App.svelte:36) — adding an optional `store` prop matching the pattern History and Journey already use is the smallest enabling change.

minors.title: CLEAN BILL — Tailwind 4 and DaisyUI 5 setup and class vocabulary are correct
minors.detail:
Recording an explicit pass so the triage does not re-derive it.

Tailwind 4: `app.css:10` uses `@import 'tailwindcss'`, not the v3 `@tailwind` directives. `vite.config.ts:20` uses the `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin; there is no `tailwind.config.js`, no `postcss.config.*`, and therefore no missing `@config`. No `@apply` in any `<style>` block (there are no `<style>` blocks at all, so the `@reference` trap does not apply). Grepped the whole of `web/src` for the renamed-utility set — no `shadow-sm`/bare `shadow`, no `rounded-sm`, no `outline-none`, no `flex-shrink-*`/`flex-grow-*`, no `bg-opacity-*`/`text-opacity-*`. No bare `focus:ring` anywhere, so the v4 1px-ring regression is not in play. Every `border`/`divide` utility carries an explicit color (`border-base-300`, `divide-base-300`, `border-primary`), so the v4 currentColor default never bites.

DaisyUI 5: configured in CSS via `@plugin 'daisyui'` + `@plugin 'daisyui/theme'`, no `require('daisyui')`. No v4 component classes — no `btn-group`, `input-group`, `form-control`, `card-compact`, `btm-nav`; `join`, `fieldset`, `card-sm`-era naming is respected (`fieldset`/`fieldset-label` used in CollectionPicker and AlbumCard). No old CSS variables (`--p`, `--b1`, `--n`, `--er`, `--pc`) anywhere. Zero hardcoded colors: no `bg-[#...]`, no `text-gray-*`, no `blue-500`; every surface uses a semantic token, and `bg-primary` surfaces get `primary-content` text from DaisyUI's own pairing.

`svelte-check --fail-on-warnings` runs clean: 0 errors, 0 warnings, so there are no unexplained a11y warnings to triage.

The one v3-era name left: bare `rounded` at App.svelte:412, App.svelte:472 and History.svelte:98. In v4 the scale shifted (`rounded-sm` -> `rounded-xs`, bare `rounded` -> `rounded-sm`); bare `rounded` still resolves as a compat alias, so it renders, but it is the old name.
minors.fix: Rename the three bare `rounded` occurrences to `rounded-sm` to match the v4 scale. Nothing else in the build config or class vocabulary needs to change.

minors.title: Native <dialog> has no accessible name
minors.detail:
`SpecCard.svelte:64` opens `` via `showModal()`. The platform supplies the dialog role, the focus trap, Escape-to-close, and focus return to the invoker — all correct, and worth noting as the right pattern. But the dialog carries no `aria-labelledby`, so it is announced as an unnamed dialog even though `

What can I upload?

` sits right inside it (SpecCard.svelte:66). WCAG 4.1.2. Also minor within this component: the `modal-backdrop` form contains `` (SpecCard.svelte:86) — a full-viewport focusable control whose label is invisible and which has no visible focus indicator. It is DaisyUI's stock pattern, so this is a note rather than a defect.
minors.fix: Give the heading an id and reference it: `<dialog aria-labelledby="spec-sheet-title" ...>` with `<h3 id="spec-sheet-title">`. Consider `aria-hidden="true"` plus `tabindex="-1"` on the backdrop close button, or `aria-label="Close"` if it should stay reachable.

minors.title: The private-lane tag form is not a <form>, so Enter does not submit and the track group has no name
minors.detail:
`AlbumCard.svelte:60-118` builds artist / album / year / N track-title fields inside a `<div class="card">` with a `type="button"` submit. Pressing Enter in any field does nothing — a keyboard user must tab past every track row to reach the button. Not a WCAG failure (the control is reachable), but it violates the platform convention users expect from a form.

Separately, the `<ul>` of track-title inputs (AlbumCard.svelte:98-111) has no group name. Each input is labelled "01 (from filename)", "02 (from filename)" — meaningful only in the context of a group that is never announced.

Also: the form has no error state of any kind. No `aria-invalid`, no `aria-describedby`, no validation message surface exists anywhere in the component, so if the year or any title is unusable the user gets nothing. That is latent rather than live (nothing currently validates), but it means 3.3.1 has no implementation to fall back on when validation lands.
minors.fix: Wrap the fields in `<form onsubmit={...}>` with the submit as `type="submit"`. Replace the track `<ul>` with `<fieldset><legend class="fieldset-legend">Track titles</legend>` so the group is named. When validation lands, tie each message to its field with `aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid` and never signal the error by border color alone (1.4.1).

minors.title: announceProgress fires "0 percent confirmed" the instant an upload starts, and re-fires unconditionally at 100%
minors.detail:
`shouldAnnounceProgress` (announce.ts:23-28) returns true whenever `lastPercent === null`, so the first tick of App's `$effect` — which runs as soon as `phase` becomes `'uploading'`, with `ackedBytes` still 0 — announces "0 percent confirmed". That is the first thing a screen-reader user hears about their upload.

It also returns true unconditionally for `percent >= 100`, so any repeat evaluation at 100 rewrites the region's text node. In practice the effect's dependencies stop changing once the files land, so this does not spam today, but it is a latent behaviour rather than a guarded one.

Separately, `lastAnnouncedJourneyState` (Journey.svelte:168) is declared `$state` and is both read and written inside the same `$effect` (lines 170-173). Svelte 5 settles this after a second pass because of the early return, but a plain `let` (no rune) is the correct tool for an effect-local guard and removes the self-dependency entirely.
minors.fix: Skip the announcement when `percent === 0` on the first call, or seed `lastPercent` to 0 when the upload starts. Change `>= 100` to fire once by tracking a `completed` flag. Change `lastAnnouncedJourneyState` from `$state` to a plain `let`.

minors.title: CLEAN BILL — motion, landmarks, page title, and drag alternatives
minors.detail:
Recording explicit passes.

Motion (2.3.3 / prefers-reduced-motion): the only two animations in `web/src` are both gated — `motion-safe:animate-pulse` on the current step label (JourneySteps.svelte:77) and `motion-safe:transition-opacity` on the in-library alert (Journey.svelte:190). DaisyUI's own 0.2s `.btn` color transition is not motion in the 2.3.3 sense. PASS.

Landmarks: `<header>` and `<main>` are both present and unique (App.svelte:321, 330). No `<nav>` is needed for a single toggle. There are no repeated blocks preceding the main content, so 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks does not require a skip link. PASS.

Focus obscured (2.4.11): the masthead is a plain `<header class="navbar">`, not sticky or fixed, so nothing can cover a focused control on scroll. PASS.

Page title (2.4.2): `index.html:6` sets `<title>dubplate</title>` and `<html lang="en">` is set at line 2. This is a standalone SPA with no router, so the SvelteKit route-announcement concern does not apply. PASS, with the note that the title never reflects state — a long upload shows "dubplate" in the tab throughout, where "Uploading — dubplate" would help a backgrounded user.

Dragging (2.5.7): `DropZone` is enhancement-only and always renders the `PickerButton` fallback; nothing in the app is drag-exclusive. PASS.
minors.fix: Optional: set `document.title` from the current phase so a backgrounded tab shows upload progress. Nothing else required.

minors.title: tusd RespectForwardedHeaders trusts a client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host, which cloudflared does not overwrite
minors.detail:
`tusCfg.RespectForwardedHeaders = true` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:261), justified in the comment by the need to emit `https://` in the absolute `Location` header. But that flag turns on host trust as well as scheme trust: tusd's `getHostAndProtocol` takes `X-Forwarded-Host` verbatim, and failing that parses `host=` out of the `Forwarded` header, with no trusted-proxy allowlist (handler/unrouted_handler.go:1348-1378, confirmed by the vendored `RespectXForwarded` / `RespectForwarded` tests). cloudflared sets `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-For` but does not strip or overwrite a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Host`, so the value reaching tusd is attacker-chosen.

Effect: `POST /upload/files/` with `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example` returns `Location: https://evil.example/upload/files/<id>`, and a tus client following it PATCHes the upload body to the attacker's host. Today that is self-directed — the attacker controls their own client — so I am rating it minor rather than major. It becomes real the moment any response containing that Location is cached, logged and replayed, or consumed by something other than the originating client, and it directly contradicts the project rule that origins come from configured values rather than request headers.
minors.fix: Strip `X-Forwarded-Host` and `Forwarded` in a middleware in front of the tus handler and set `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` yourself from the configured public origin, keeping `RespectForwardedHeaders: true` only so tusd picks up the scheme you control. tusd's own docs make the same point: enable it only behind a proxy that overwrites those headers.

minors.title: sanitizeFilename does not reject "..", defused only by an incidental Stat check
minors.detail:
`sanitizeFilename` rejects the empty string and `"."` but says nothing about `".."` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:510-522). A `filename` metadata value of `".."`, or `"anything/.."` which the last-slash strip reduces to `".."`, therefore flows through as the sanitized name.

It is not currently exploitable, and only by accident: in `assembleUpload`, `filepath.Join(sessionDir, "..")` resolves to UploadsDir, which always exists, so the duplicate-name guard at upload.go:596-600 rewrites the destination to `sessionDir/<uploadID>-..` — a harmless literal. Remove or reorder that Stat check, or add a caller that joins the name without it, and this becomes a write outside the session directory. The function's own doc comment claims "no directory traversal" and "a caller can always join the result under a directory without a second check", which is not true as written.
minors.fix: Extend the rejection to `name == ".."` alongside `""` and `"."`, so the doc comment's promise holds independent of any caller's Stat.

minors.title: The Access email claim is used as an identity key without normalization, while roster lookup is case-insensitive
minors.detail:
`enforceAccess` puts the raw claim into the request context: `next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(WithEmail(r.Context(), email)))` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/serve.go:312), with no lowercasing or trimming. That exact string then becomes the identity key for every comparison in the system: `Session.Email` and the cross-user checks against it (upload.go:387, upload.go:914), the `email` metadata stamped on each tus upload and compared byte-for-byte in `enforceUploadOwnership` (upload.go:348) and `preTerminate` (upload.go:474), the ledger's `Email` field, `Ledger.History(email)`'s exact-match filter (internal/ledger/ledger.go:265-269), and `sessionsForEmail` (api.go:342).

Meanwhile the one place that does normalize is the roster: `DirNameFor` lowercases and trims (internal/config/contributors.go:93-99). So the system is simultaneously case-insensitive about who may enter and case-sensitive about what is theirs.

Failure mode: if the identity provider ever returns a different casing for the same human across sign-ins (a different IdP, a changed directory record, an SSO migration), that person's in-flight upload starts 404-ing for them at `enforceUploadOwnership`, their `/api/journey` polls 404, and `/api/history` silently splits into two disjoint histories with no error anywhere to explain it.
minors.fix: Normalize once at the trust boundary — `email = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(email))` in `verifiedIdentity` or immediately before `WithEmail` — so every downstream comparison and every ledger record uses the same canonical form the roster already uses.

minors.title: JWKS refresh holds the verifier mutex across the network fetch and replaces the key cache wholesale
minors.detail:
`refreshLocked` is called with `v.mu` held (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/access/access.go:141) and performs the full HTTP round trip inside the lock (access.go:155-197), bounded only by the 10s `jwksTimeout`. Every concurrent `Verify` blocks in `key()` behind that same mutex, so one slow certs endpoint stalls all authentication for up to ten seconds — with `ReadHeaderTimeout` at 10s and the page polling every 5s, that is enough to make the whole app appear hung.

Second issue in the same function: `v.keys = keys` replaces the cache wholesale (access.go:195). If the endpoint ever answers 200 with an unexpected body, or with a key set whose entries all fail the `Kty != "RSA"` filter or the `rsaPublicKeyFromJWK` decode (both `continue` silently, access.go:186-192), the verifier ends up with an empty map and no memory of the keys that were working a moment earlier. The `jwksRefreshCooldown` then blocks any retry for five minutes (access.go:138-140), so a single malformed response locks every family member out for the full window.
minors.fix: Fetch outside the lock (take the lock only to swap the result in, using a single-flight guard so concurrent unknown-kid lookups do not stampede). Merge new keys into the existing map, or refuse to install an empty result and keep the previous set, so a bad response degrades to "stale keys" instead of "no keys".

minors.title: JWK exponent decode silently truncates via Int64, and no modulus size floor is enforced
minors.detail:
`rsaPublicKeyFromJWK` builds the exponent as `int(new(big.Int).SetBytes(eBytes).Int64())` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/access/access.go:212). `big.Int.Int64` is undefined for values that do not fit and truncates; on a 32-bit build the outer `int()` truncates again, and either can yield a nonsensical or negative exponent that is then installed in the key map under a real `kid`. There is likewise no check that the modulus is non-zero or of a sane bit length.

The source is Cloudflare's own certs endpoint over TLS, so this is low risk and I am not claiming an attack. It is an unvalidated parse in the one package whose entire job is deciding who gets in, and the silent `continue` on decode failure (access.go:190-192) means a malformed key is indistinguishable from an absent one in logs.
minors.fix: Reject a JWK whose exponent does not fit in an int or whose modulus is below a minimum bit length (2048), and log the rejection rather than silently skipping it. `jwt.ParseRSAPublicKeyFromPEM`-adjacent helpers or a maintained JWKS library would carry these checks for you.

minors.title: The private collection is never validated as a member of the configured collection list, so the private lane can be advertised but unusable
minors.detail:
`NewEngine` defaults `PrivateCollection` to `"Private Recordings"` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:214-216) and its own doc comment states the requirement: "It must also appear in [config.Config.Collections] for [validCollection] to admit a session created against it" (upload.go:56-59). Nothing checks it. `NewServer` does not, `NewEngine` does not, and `internal/checks`/doctor does not.

Meanwhile `GET /api/config` publishes `private_collection` to the client unconditionally (serve.go:403), so the UI will offer a lane the server rejects with a 400 from `validCollection` (upload.go:400-402 for the ZIP path, session.go:260-262 for the explicit path). Observed on the running dev instance: `{"collections":[""], ..., "private_collection":"Private Recordings"}` — advertised, unreachable.

The inverse matters too, given the private lane is the one branch that skips the tag-check probe entirely (upload.go:642-646): the lane is selected by exact string equality on a config value, so a collection renamed in `DUBPLATE_COLLECTIONS` without the matching `PrivateCollection` update silently moves albums from the no-probe lane to the probe lane or back, with no startup error.
minors.fix: Have `NewServer` (or `NewEngine`) return a startup error when `privateCollection` is not in `cfg.Collections`, and add the same assertion to `dubplate doctor`. A custody-policy lane selected by string equality deserves a fail-fast check, not a runtime 400.

minors.title: Terminating an upload does not release its reserved session slot, wedging the session until the 24h sweep
minors.detail:
`Session.reserve` increments `sess.reserved` and hands out a slot (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/session.go:138-147); `preTerminate` performs the ownership check and returns, with no path back to decrement it (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:472-478). `reserve` refuses once `reserved >= ExpectedFiles` (session.go:141), and completion by count requires `doneUploads >= ExpectedFiles` (session.go:160).

So a contributor who starts a file and cancels it — a normal thing to do when you pick the wrong track, and something a tus client does on abort — permanently burns one of their declared slots. The session can then never reach its expected count on its own. Their only escape is `POST /api/session/{id}/finish`, which requires `doneCount() > 0` (upload.go:918-921), so a session where the *first* file was cancelled is completely stuck and holds one of the three `MaxSessionsPerUser` slots for the full 24h `PartialTTL`.
minors.fix: Decrement `sess.reserved` in `preTerminate` (under the session mutex, guarding against double-terminate) so a cancelled upload returns its slot, and let a session with zero completed uploads be abandoned explicitly rather than only by timeout.

minors.title: /api/history is unpaginated and re-reads the entire ledger file O(sessions) times per request, on a polled endpoint
minors.detail:
`Ledger` holds no cache: `History` and `Session` each call `readAll`, which opens and scans the whole JSONL file every time (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/ledger/ledger.go:259-305). `handleHistory` then, per session id, calls `j.advance` (two `Ledger.Session` calls, ledger reads #1 and #2 — see api.go:186 and api.go:204) and `journey.Resolve` (a third, journey.go:78), plus `hasEarlierUnsettled` does one more per other live session (api.go:311). That is at least 3N full-file reads for N sessions in a contributor's history, with no `LIMIT` and no pagination — `handleHistory` returns every session the email has ever touched (api.go:132-163).

The ledger is append-only and never rotated, so both N and the file size grow monotonically for the life of the estate, and the page polls this endpoint. Quadratic growth on a polled endpoint is the kind of thing that is invisible for a month and then makes the uploader feel broken. It is also a cheap amplification lever for any on-roster caller.
minors.fix: Read the ledger once per request and pass the parsed slice down to `advance`, `Resolve`, and `hasEarlierUnsettled` instead of letting each re-read the file. Cap the response (most-recent N sessions) and paginate the rest.

minors.title: Session-quota and free-space admission checks are check-then-act races
minors.detail:
`handleCreateSession` calls `e.sessions.countActive(email)` and then `e.sessions.create(...)` as two separate operations with no lock spanning them (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:883-888); `preCreate` has the identical pattern (upload.go:403-409). Each takes `Store.mu` internally and releases it, so N concurrent requests can all observe `countActive == MaxSessionsPerUser - 1` and all proceed.

Same shape for the free-space admission at upload.go:421-428: `archive.FreeSpace` is sampled and compared against the floor, then the upload is created. Concurrent `preCreate` calls each subtract only their own `hook.Upload.Size` from the same snapshot, so K simultaneous creates can collectively admit K times more than the floor allows and push the filesystem below `FreeFloorGB`.

At family scale this is unlikely to be hit deliberately, but the multi-file upload path issues its creates in parallel by design, so the free-space race is reachable by ordinary use rather than only by an attacker.
minors.fix: Move the quota check inside `Store.create` under the single `Store.mu` acquisition so count-and-insert is atomic. For free space, track bytes admitted-but-not-yet-written on the Engine and subtract that reservation from the `FreeSpace` sample, rather than trusting an unsynchronized statfs.

minors.title: POST /api/session returns raw internal error text, breaking the reject-wording contract
minors.detail:
`handleCreateSession` responds with `http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:890). The errors it can surface are `"serve: invalid album name: \"<raw input>\""` (session.go:94), `"serve: unknown collection: \"...\""` (session.go:261), and `"serve: expected_files must be at least 1, got N"` (session.go:258). All three reach the contributor verbatim, package prefix and all, echoing up to 4 KiB of their own input back at them.

Not an XSS: Go's `http.Error` sets `text/plain; charset=utf-8` plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. The problem is contract. CLAUDE.md records that "Reject wording is contract (internal/reject / friendly_reason): the uploader page and emails share it verbatim", and every other rejection on this surface honors that — `preCreate` returns `reasonError(reject.ReasonTooManySessions, ...)` and `reasonError(reject.ReasonNoSpace, ...)` with the proper `{code, friendly, next_step}` body (upload.go:404, upload.go:427), and the quota path in this very handler uses `writeJSON(w, 429, reject.ReasonTooManySessions)` six lines earlier (upload.go:884). Only the validation path leaks Go error strings.
minors.fix: Map the three sentinels (`ErrInvalidAlbum`, `ErrUnknownCollection`, the expected-files error) to `reject.Reason` values via `errors.Is` and return them through `writeJSON` in the same shape as the sibling branch, so the page has one thing to parse and the contributor sees family-facing copy.

minors.title: No rate limiting on any endpoint
minors.detail:
Nothing in `internal/serve/` limits request rate, per identity or per IP. `POST /api/session` can be called in a loop (bounded only by `MaxSessionsPerUser`, but each rejected call still costs a full `Store` scan in `countActive`); `POST /files/` create can be called for every reserved slot; `GET /api/history` and `GET /api/journey/{id}` each trigger the multiple full ledger reads described above plus an outbound Navidrome call, and are designed to be polled; `POST /api/stream/probe` holds a connection forever.

The mitigating fact is real and worth stating: Cloudflare Access gates the whole surface, so an attacker must already be an authenticated roster member. That makes this a robustness concern rather than an internet-facing one — but the amplification factors on the journey/history endpoints mean a single misbehaving or looping browser tab is enough to degrade the service for everyone.
minors.fix: Add a small per-identity token bucket in `enforceAccess` covering the write endpoints and the polled read endpoints, or configure a Cloudflare Rate Limiting rule on the `/upload` path so the limit is enforced before the request reaches the origin. See the OWASP Denial of Service Cheat Sheet.

minors.title: Roster-absent HTML page is returned with 200 for asset and near-miss API paths
minors.detail:
`isAPIOrFilesPath` matches only the prefixes `/api/` and `/files/` (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/serve.go:318-320), so `enforceAccess` treats everything else as a document request and answers a roster-absent identity with the warm HTML page at `200 OK` (serve.go:305-309).

That means a roster-absent user's browser receives `text/html` with status 200 for `/upload/assets/index-<hash>.js` and `/upload/assets/index-<hash>.css`. Since those are hashed, immutable assets served with `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` (serve.go:205), a browser or intermediary that caches the response caches HTML under a JavaScript URL for a year; once the user is added to the roster, the app can fail to load with a syntax error and no obvious cause.

The path-prefix gap also catches the exact strings `/api` and `/files` with no trailing slash, which get the HTML page rather than the JSON failure body an API client expects. Neither is an authorization bypass — every path still requires a verified identity — but the response shape is wrong for the resource.
minors.fix: Serve the warm page only for requests that actually accept HTML (a navigation request, or `Accept` containing `text/html`) and return a 403 with the JSON failure body otherwise; and set `Cache-Control: no-store` on the roster-absent response so it can never be cached under an asset URL.

minors.title: tusd runs with the default permissive CORS policy rather than a pinned origin
minors.detail:
`thandler.Config` is built without a `Cors` field (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:245-265), so tusd installs `DefaultCorsConfig`, which is `AllowOrigin: regexp.MustCompile(".*")` (handler/config.go:143-146). Every tus response therefore echoes whatever `Origin` the caller sent into `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`.

The default also sets `AllowCredentials: false`, so a browser will not attach the Access cookie to a cross-origin request and cannot read the response — which is why I am rating this minor rather than major. But the app is served from exactly one known origin, that origin is already in config as `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, and leaving a wildcard reflector on an authenticated upload API is the kind of default that stops being harmless the first time someone flips `AllowCredentials` or fronts the service differently.
minors.fix: Set `tusCfg.Cors` explicitly with `AllowOrigin` anchored to the configured public origin (`^https://music\.907\.life$`, built from config rather than hardcoded) and `AllowCredentials: false`, matching the same origin the CSRF check should use.

refuted.title: Ghost buttons are invisible on the dark ground — two of the three push-back recovery actions don't look clickable
refuted.detail:
`btn-ghost` sets no background and no border, so on base-100 it renders as bare bold text. Confirmed in the probe render of the pushed-back alert: "Upload to Private Recordings" is a filled blue button, but "Fix the names and retry" and "Add it to MusicBrainz" appear as plain bold sentences with no box, no border, nothing distinguishing them from the paragraph above. Same for "Your uploads" in the masthead — in the idle capture it has no box; it only gains a visible outline in the history capture because that shot caught the focus ring.

This is an interaction-honesty failure at the point of highest user frustration: the album was pushed back, and two of the three ways out do not read as controls.
refuted.fix: Use `btn-outline` (or a bordered soft variant) for the secondary recovery actions and the nav control so they carry a visible edge on the dark ground. Reserve ghost for controls sitting on an already-tinted surface.

refuted.title: The spine claims "Checked -- every file is CD-quality FLAC" before the ZIP has been checked
refuted.detail: Journey mounts as soon as the bytes land and its 'finishing' view hardcodes statuses `['complete', 'complete', 'current', 'upcoming']`, so step 2 renders complete with the sublabel "every file is CD-quality FLAC" while `finishSession` is still running the unpack and the gate server-side. On the ZIP path the page told the user seconds earlier, in its own words, "We check the tracks once the zip finishes uploading." It then immediately claims the check passed. If the gate fails, the spine flips a completed green step back to an error. Section 3 anticipated exactly this window and ratified a step-2-current sublabel for it, "unpacking and checking the tracks", which no component implements.
refuted.fix: Give 'finishing' the honest shape `['complete', 'current', 'upcoming', 'upcoming']` and pass a flag down to JourneySteps so step 2's sublabel is "unpacking and checking the tracks" while current (ZIP path) and "every file is CD-quality FLAC" once complete. Advance step 3 to current only once the finish probe reaches the match stage.
refuted.verifier_reasoning:
REFUTED — the finding's mechanism does not survive contact with the code. Its one true half is a sub-second cosmetic window, not a major defect.

What is confirmed:
- Journey.svelte:86-102 does hardcode 'finishing' as ['complete','complete','current','upcoming'], and JourneySteps.svelte:36 gives step 2 the sublabel "every file is CD-quality FLAC".
- App.svelte:208/442 mounts Journey once `allFilesLanded`, and Journey.svelte:120-122 calls store.finishSession on mount.
- format-rejected maps to ['complete','error',...], so on a rejection step 2 does go green-then-error.
- docs/superpowers/research/passb-copy-final.md:103 does carry an unimplemented string ("ZIP-path checking sublabel (step 2 current): 'unpacking and checking the tracks'"); grep finds it nowhere in web/src.

What is refuted, and why it kills the finding:

1. "while finishSession is still running the unpack and the gate server-side" is false. The unpack and the gate do not run during /finish. internal/serve/upload.go:441-466 (`preFinish`, tusd's PreFinishResponseCallback) calls `assembleUpload` — which for a ZIP runs `intake.CheckZIP` and `archive.Extract` (upload.go:542-585) — inside the last PATCH request, and then, once every slot has reported, runs `completeSession` in that same request ("a lone ZIP's completion IS its album's verdict, delivered in the same request"). The client sets a file to 'ok' only in tus `onSuccess` (upload.svelte.ts:482-483), which fires after that PATCH response returns. So by the time the spine can render at all, the unpack and the format gate have already finished on the server. The /finish POST Journey then fires is an idempotent read: `completeSession` sees `completeOnce()` false and returns the cached outcome via `waitOutcome` (upload.go:625-632), and `discard` (upload.go:755) does not remove the session from the registry, so even a rejected session answers immediately.

2. "The page told the user seconds earlier 'We check the tracks once the zip finishes uploading.' It then immediately claims the check passed." Backwards. App.svelte:452-455 shows that line in the NOT-yet-landed branch — it is on screen for exactly the window in which the extract and check actually run (the blocking final PATCH). The sentence is honest and the spine only replaces it afterward.

3. "Section 3 anticipated exactly this window ... which no component implements." The mockup is the layout authority, and ref-3-uploading-4-journey.jpg shows the journey spine with step 2 already a green check reading "every file is CD-quality FLAC" and step 3 "Matching" as current — precisely the built shape. The unimplemented copy line describes a client-side state the built architecture does not have: there is no moment where the spine is mounted while a ZIP is unpacking.

Residual, and it is minor at most: between mount and the /finish response, the page green-ticks step 2 without yet holding the verdict, and on a format rejection that tick flips to error. The work was genuinely done; only the answer is in flight, over one round-trip of an already-decided outcome. The only path that lengthens that window is a partial resume from History (fewer files re-picked than the session's ExpectedFiles), where /finish would trigger `completeSession` for real — and even there each landed file was checked in its own PATCH, and the long part is the MusicBrainz probe, which the spine honestly shows as step 3 current.

The proposed fix would also actively regress fidelity: giving 'finishing' ['complete','current','upcoming','upcoming'] would show step 2 as in-progress after the check has already completed, and would contradict the ratified section 4 mockup.

refuted.title: Residue (b): the mobile copy register is keyed on isIOSSafari(), so Android phones get the desktop SpecCard and lose the "What can I upload?" sheet
refuted.detail:
`const isIOS = isIOSSafari()` (App.svelte:51) drives two different decisions that do not share an axis:

1. **The picker gesture hint** (App.svelte:375-382): "tap ⋯ in the picker, then Select" is genuinely iOS-Safari-specific, and `isIOSSafari()` is the right key. `platform.ts:32-41` correctly handles the iPadOS desktop-class UA via `maxTouchPoints`, so the stated rationale (an iPad's wide viewport slipping past a CSS breakpoint) holds for this one.

2. **The format-panel copy register** (App.svelte:372, `variant={isIOS ? 'mobile' : 'desktop'}`): this is a *viewport/pointer* concern, not a browser-engine one. On a narrow Android phone `isIOS` is false, so the user gets SpecCard's desktop paragraph — "Upload a whole album: a .zip or its files" — instead of the phone register "From a phone or iPad, a .zip of the album is easiest", **and loses the "What can I upload?" detail sheet entirely** (SpecCard.svelte:56-88), which is the only place the full FLAC/size/cover-art/extras rules appear on a small screen. The mockup's section-2 iPhone reference is the layout authority for a phone-width viewport regardless of vendor.

DropZone's own hint is correctly handled — `hidden ... md:flex` (DropZone.svelte:106) means the "Drop an album anywhere on this page" line and its "or" divider are already hidden below 768px on Android, so that half is not a defect. The residual defect is SpecCard's register (and the folder button, filed separately).
refuted.fix: Split the two axes. Keep `isIOSSafari()` for the iOS multi-select gesture hint and the extension-first `accept` rationale. Derive the SpecCard register from the viewport instead: either render both variants with `hidden md:block` / `md:hidden` wrappers (matching DropZone's existing convention and avoiding a reactive media query altogether), or add `isCoarsePointer()` to lib/platform.ts as `matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches` and use `variant={isIOS || isCoarse ? 'mobile' : 'desktop'}`.
refuted.verifier_reasoning:
The mechanism is accurately described but the "defect" framing does not survive contact with the two authorities and the captures. Refuted as a major.

WHAT IS TRUE (code confirmed):
- /var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/web/src/App.svelte:51 `const isIOS = isIOSSafari()`, and :372 `<SpecCard variant={isIOS ? 'mobile' : 'desktop'} .../>`. On Android, isIOS is false (platform.test.ts:62-63 asserts exactly that for the Android Chrome UA), so Android phones get the desktop SpecCard branch (SpecCard.svelte:39-48) and never the mobile branch with the "What can I upload?" dialog (SpecCard.svelte:49-88, the only showModal in the codebase).

WHY IT IS NOT A DEFECT:

1. The finding's stated layout authority says the opposite of what the finding claims. The reviewer argues "the mockup's section-2 iPhone reference is the layout authority for a phone-width viewport regardless of vendor." The mockup's own section header, visible in reference/ref-1-desktop-idle-full.jpg, reads "2 · IPAD / IPHONE — SELECTION". It is labeled by device family, not by viewport. The string authority agrees: passb-copy-final.md section 1 has exactly two register headings, "Desktop:" and "iPad / iPhone:" (line 47). Keying the register on isIOSSafari() implements the contract as written; keying it on a breakpoint would be the deviation.

2. The mobile register is one indivisible iOS block, so splitting only SpecCard off it produces an incoherent hybrid. The contract's "iPad / iPhone" list is: the shortened subhead, the .zip-first format panel, the button labeled "Choose from Files" (the iOS Files app by name), the "tap ⋯ in the picker, then Select" gesture, and the "What can I upload?" sheet. The reviewer concedes items 4 and 5 of that list are correctly iOS-keyed. Applying its own fix would give an Android phone "From a phone or iPad, a .zip of the album is easiest" sitting above a button labeled "Choose files" and a "Choose a folder" button, a combination neither the mockup nor the copy contract describes anywhere. The current Android rendering is at least a coherent, contract-defined register.

3. The core substantive claim is factually wrong. The finding says the sheet "is the only place the full FLAC/size/cover-art/extras rules appear on a small screen." The desktop panel Android actually gets carries lossless FLAC/CD quality, whole album, ".zip or its files", the max size, and cover art optional — four of the five facts, in the contract's own words. Only "MP3, AAC, and other lossy files can't go in" and "Booklets and other extras ride along" are sheet-exclusive, and both are restatements a user does not need before picking. No format rule is lost.

4. The already-captured 390px and 320px screenshots ARE the Android-phone rendering, and they are clean. The captures were taken in desktop-UA Chromium, so isIOS was false and the desktop branch rendered. idle-phone-390.png shows the full format card wrapping cleanly, "Choose files", the "One album at a time" hint, and "Choose a folder" — no overflow, no truncation, no orphaned drop hint (DropZone.svelte:106 `hidden ... md:flex` hides it, which the reviewer concedes). There is no visual failure to fix.

5. It is an already-adjudicated, logged residue, not a discovery. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-dubplate-uploader.md:906-911 records verbatim: "App's mobile register now keys on isIOSSafari() instead of the md: breakpoint: narrow Android phones get the desktop register with DropZone's drop hint hidden below md. Defensible per the contract's 'iPad / iPhone' naming, but untested — exercise it in the fidelity chain's device matrix." The considered ruling was already made, with a verification owner assigned (the device matrix). Re-raising it as a major would reopen a decision on weaker grounds than the ones already recorded.

Residual value: there is a real, minor question of whether Android phones should eventually get a phone register, but that is a copy-contract amendment (adding an "Android phone" register, or renaming "iPad / iPhone" to "phone"), not a code fix, and it belongs to the device-matrix check the plan already schedules. Nothing here is major and nothing would embarrass in front of family.

refuted.title: Residue (b), second half: "Choose a folder" renders on Chrome for Android where directory picking does not work
refuted.detail:
`supportsDirectorySelect()` probes `'webkitdirectory' in input`. The attribute is present in Blink's `HTMLInputElement` IDL on Android, but Android's document picker offers no directory selection — the input degrades to an ordinary file picker. Combined with the `isIOSSafari()` keying above, a narrow Android phone lands in the desktop register (App.svelte:389-400) and is shown a full-width "Choose a folder" button that opens a plain file picker. The button is dead weight at best and confusing at worst on the smallest viewport, where it is also the third stacked control.

I have not verified this on a physical Android device — worth confirming before the fix lands, but the IDL-presence-vs-behavior gap is well documented for `webkitdirectory`.
refuted.fix: Gate the folder affordance on a non-touch pointer as well as the IDL probe: `const supportsFolderSelect = supportsDirectorySelect() && !matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches;`, or wrap the folder button in a `hidden md:block` container so it never renders below the desktop breakpoint. Extend platform.test.ts to cover the new predicate.
refuted.verifier_reasoning:
REFUTED on both its factual premise and its design premise.

1. The behavioral claim is stale by ~20 months. The finding asserts that on Android "the input degrades to an ordinary file picker" and that only the IDL attribute is present. MDN browser-compat-data (`api/HTMLInputElement.json`, `webkitdirectory.__compat.support`) records exactly that state as HISTORICAL, not current:
   - `chrome_android`: `version_added: "132"` with NO `partial_implementation` flag (full support). The two superseded ranges are the finding's description: 18-131 partial, note "The property reflects the attribute, but users cannot choose a directory, only individual files (crbug 40248532)"; and 131-132 partial, "if a user selects a directory, the browser crashes (crbug 376834374)".
   - `firefox_android`: full since 142. `samsunginternet_android` and `webview_android`: `"mirror"` (i.e. Chrome Android's full support).
   - MDN marks the feature Baseline "Newly available" since August 2025 — "works across the latest devices and browser versions", which by definition includes the mobile browsers.
   Chrome Android 132 shipped January 2025. Any Android phone a family member is using in September 2026 picks directories correctly. The finding itself flagged that it was reasoning from a documented gap it had not verified; the documentation says the gap closed.

2. The proposed fix would break the ratified spec, not fix a defect. The plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-dubplate-uploader.md) names folder-select as a **desktop/Android** affordance in two places:
   - line 64: "ZIP is the primary path on every platform, folder-select a feature-detected desktop/Android extra hidden on iOS"
   - line 758 (U10 acceptance criteria): "folder-select renders only where `webkitdirectory` feature-detects (hidden, not disabled, on iOS Safari -- WebKit 271705 confirms it unimplemented)"
   App.svelte:50 (`const supportsFolderSelect = supportsDirectorySelect();`) plus the `{#if supportsFolderSelect}` block at 389-400 implements that criterion literally. Gating on `!matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')` or wrapping in `hidden md:block` would DELETE a spec'd Android affordance. `hidden md:block` would additionally kill it in a narrow desktop window, and `pointer: coarse` would kill it on touchscreen laptops and Windows tablets, which report coarse pointers and pick directories fine. Both fixes are regressions.

3. The crowding half is overstated. /var/home/glw907/.claude/jobs/daef7196/tmp/captures/idle-phone-390.png (the desktop register at phone width — chromium-shot is not iOS Safari, so this capture IS what an Android phone renders) shows two stacked buttons, not three controls: "Choose files" (primary), the hint line, then the outline "Choose a folder". The column is uncluttered with large vertical whitespace below. No collection picker renders at this state.

The code claims in the finding are accurate as far as they go (platform.ts:16 is a bare `'webkitdirectory' in input` IDL probe; App.svelte keys the register on `isIOSSafari()` alone, so Android lands in the desktop register). Those facts are correct and deliberate — the plan's own residue list at line ~905 records the isIOSSafari keying as an accepted, "defensible per the contract's 'iPad / iPhone' naming" decision to exercise in the device matrix. What the finding builds on top of them does not hold.

Adjacent observation for the parent, NOT a defect and not this finding: the same BCD entry shows `safari_ios` gained full `webkitdirectory` support in 18.4 (previously partial, "property can be set but has no effect", WebKit 271705 — the exact bug the plan's gate-3 ruling cites). So the plan's premise that iOS can never pick directories is now also stale. It does not change page behavior, because iOS is routed by the `isIOS` branch at App.svelte:375 rather than by the probe, so the contracted iOS register still renders as specified. Worth knowing only if someone later revisits the iOS copy.

refuted.title: Focus indicator on every btn-primary is invisible in both themes (WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible, Level A)
refuted.detail:
DaisyUI 5 emits `.btn:focus-visible{outline-width:2px;outline-style:solid}` with no `outline-color`, so the ring paints in `currentColor`. On `.btn-primary` currentColor is `--color-primary-content`. With `outline-offset:2px` the ring lands outside the button, on the page background.

Measured against the theme values in app.css:
- dark: primary-content `oklch(20% .02 240)` = #0e171e against base-100 `oklch(26% 0 0)` = #242424 -> **1.16:1** (1.04:1 on a base-200 card).
- light: primary-content `oklch(98% .01 265)` = #f5f8ff against base-100 #ffffff -> **1.06:1** (1.00:1 on base-200).

The affected controls are the app's primary CTAs: OutcomeAlert's "Upload to Private Recordings" (line 45) and "Try again" (line 61), AlbumCard's submit (line 114), Journey's "Open in Navidrome" (line 194). A keyboard user tabbing the pushed-back recovery flow gets no visible focus at all. `PickerButton.svelte:52` already solves this correctly with `focus-within:outline-primary focus-within:outline-2 focus-within:outline-offset-2` (9.94:1 on the dark ground) — that treatment simply was not applied anywhere else.
refuted.fix: Set an explicit focus-ring color once, globally, rather than per call site: in `app.css` add `.btn:focus-visible{outline-color:var(--color-primary);outline-offset:2px}` (and a base-content variant for `.btn-primary` if primary-on-primary reads poorly), or set `--color-primary-content` aside and give every `btn-primary` the same `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-primary` PickerButton uses. Verify the chosen ring clears 3:1 against both base-100 and base-200 in both themes (1.4.11).
refuted.verifier_reasoning:
REFUTED — the finding's core premise is factually wrong.

The reviewer read only `.btn:focus-visible{isolation:isolate;outline-width:2px;outline-style:solid}` and inferred that, with no `outline-color` in that rule, the ring falls back to `currentColor` (= `--color-primary-content` on `.btn-primary`). DaisyUI declares the outline color in the *base* `.btn` rule instead, not in the `:focus-visible` rule.

Evidence from the actually-served stylesheet (`/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/web/dist/assets/index-IQcOmWuR.css`, confirmed identical to what the live dev binary serves at `http://127.0.0.1:8090/upload/assets/index-IQcOmWuR.css`, and matching `web/node_modules/daisyui/daisyui.css`, DaisyUI 5.7.25):

- `.btn{ … outline-offset:2px … }` and a later `.btn{ … outline-color:var(--btn-color,var(--color-base-content)) … }`
- `.btn-primary{--btn-color:var(--color-primary);--btn-fg:var(--color-primary-content);--btn-soft-bg:initial}`

`--btn-color` is set on the same element by `.btn-primary`, so `var(--btn-color, …)` in `.btn`'s `outline-color` resolves to `--color-primary`. The focus ring paints in **primary**, which is exactly the color the finding praises `PickerButton.svelte:52` for applying manually. I also grepped every `outline-color` declaration in the built sheet: only three exist — the `.btn` one above, `.focus-within\:outline-primary:focus-within{outline-color:var(--color-primary)}`, and two `.card` rules. Nothing sets a `currentColor` outline on buttons.

Contrast, recomputed from the `app.css` theme tokens (same oklch→sRGB math the reviewer used — my `--color-primary-content` numbers reproduce theirs exactly at 1.16 / 1.04 / 1.06, so the arithmetic was right and only the color choice was wrong):

- dark `--color-primary` oklch(85% .08 240) = #9ed5fd → **9.94:1** vs base-100 #242424, **11.08:1** vs base-200
- light `--color-primary` oklch(45% .19 265) = #1f47bc → **7.83:1** vs base-100 #ffffff, **7.39:1** vs base-200

All four clear 3:1 (1.4.11) with large margin, in both themes, on both grounds. WCAG 2.4.7 is satisfied: `.btn:focus-visible` gives a 2px solid primary ring at 2px offset on every `btn-primary` cited — OutcomeAlert.svelte:45 and :61, AlbumCard.svelte:114, Journey.svelte:194 (I read all four; each is a plain `class="btn btn-primary"` on a real `<button>`/`<a>`, so `:focus-visible` applies directly).

The PickerButton case is not "the treatment that was not applied elsewhere" — it is a different problem. There the focusable element is the visually-hidden `<input type="file">` *inside* the `<label>`, so `.btn:focus-visible` never matches the label; PickerButton needs `focus-within:*` to move the ring onto the label. It restates the color because the utility set requires it, not because the default color is broken.

No change is warranted. Applying the proposed global `.btn:focus-visible{outline-color:var(--color-primary)}` would additionally be a regression risk: it would override DaisyUI's per-variant `--btn-color` ring for `btn-ghost`, `btn-outline`, `btn-error`, etc., flattening every button's focus ring to primary. It also violates the app.css header constraint that only DaisyUI theme tokens are set there, never DaisyUI's own class names.

refuted.title: NAMED CHECK 2 — live regions: journey/progress announcements are wired correctly, but four App-level state transitions are silent
refuted.detail:
VERDICT: the plumbing is sound; the coverage has holes.

What is correct and verified end to end: the single `role="status" aria-live="polite"` div renders unconditionally at `App.svelte:332`, inside `<main>`, from first paint and across every phase and both views — it is `sr-only` (position:absolute) so it does not consume a flex gap slot. `announcer.attach()` runs in `onMount` (App.svelte:89-92) before any announcement can fire. The same instance is threaded into `Journey` as a prop (App.svelte:447), so there is exactly one region, never a second one mounted late. Progress: `tus.ts` `onAcked` -> `entry.ackedBytes` (`upload.svelte.ts:479-480`, `$state`) -> App's `$effect` (App.svelte:190-200) -> `announceProgress`, throttled to >=25-point deltas by `shouldAnnounceProgress`. That chain is real and fires on transitions. Journey state changes announce twice over: `announceForViewMode()` in `runFinish`'s finally (Journey.svelte:139) covers matched / pushed-back / probe-unavailable / format-rejected, and the `$effect` at Journey.svelte:169-181 covers the polled queued / stalled / in-library transitions, with in-library correctly routed through the distinct `announceCompletion`.

The gaps:
1. Four App-level phase/view transitions never announce: `idle -> tagging` (App.svelte:137), `idle -> uploading` (App.svelte:144), the resume path's `-> uploading` (App.svelte:279), and the `view` swap between upload and history (App.svelte:325). Each of these replaces the entire contents of `<main>` with no announcement, no focus move, and no heading to land on. A screen-reader user who activates "Your uploads" hears nothing at all and has no cue that the page changed (4.1.3, and 2.4.3 for the orientation loss).
2. `idle -> preflight-rejected` (App.svelte:128) relies on the `role="alert"` div at App.svelte:404 being inserted into the DOM. Dynamically-inserted `role="alert"` containers are the pattern the guidance warns about; it works in most engines but is exactly the case the pre-existing region exists to cover.
3. Double-announcement: Journey both writes to the shared region AND renders a `role="alert"`/`role="status"` OutcomeAlert carrying the same message (OutcomeAlert.svelte:33, 55, 64, 73; Journey.svelte:190, 219). A pushed-back album announces "No MusicBrainz match for this album." from the live region and then the alert's full body from the injected alert.
refuted.fix: Add `announcer.announceState(...)` calls at the four silent transitions — e.g. "Tag this album", "Uploading N tracks", "Your uploads" — mirroring the copy contract's own wording. For the view swap, additionally move focus to the `History` `<h2>` (give it `tabindex="-1"`) so keyboard orientation follows the region change. To kill the double-announce, drop `role="alert"`/`role="status"` from the OutcomeAlert and Journey alert containers and let the one shared region carry the announcement (the alerts stay visually identical, and their headings become reachable).
refuted.verifier_reasoning:
REFUTED at the stated severity (major). The finding's factual spine is correct but its load-bearing supporting claims are wrong, and what survives is minor polish, not a major defect. What I confirmed: - The plumbing description is accurate. `/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/web/src/App.svelte:332` renders the single `role="status" aria-live="polite"` div unconditionally inside `
`, outside every `{#if}`; `announcer.attach()` runs in `onMount` (App.svelte:89-92); the same instance is passed to `Journey` (App.svelte:447). Grep for `announcer\.` across `web/src` (non-test) returns exactly: App.svelte:81 (construct), :91 (attach), :199 (`announceProgress`), :447 (prop), plus Journey.svelte:149/152/155/158/175/177/179. So the literal claim "no `announceState` fires at the four App-level transitions" is a true code fact. Where the finding fails: 1. "no heading to land on" is false for two of the four transitions it cites, and those are the two it argues hardest about. `idle -> tagging` renders `AlbumCard`, whose first content is `

Tag this album

` (AlbumCard.svelte:62). The `view` swap renders `History`, which is a `
` whose first child is `

Your uploads

` (History.svelte:93) — a landmark plus a heading, exactly the orientation target the finding says is missing. Only the `-> uploading` transitions genuinely land on headingless content (JourneySteps is a `
    `, FileRow list, WakeLockBar — no heading). 2. "A screen-reader user who activates 'Your uploads' hears nothing at all" is false as written. The toggle is a single button (App.svelte:325-327) whose own accessible name flips from "Your uploads" to "Back to upload" while focus stays on it; NVDA/JAWS announce an accessible-name change on the focused element. The user gets a cue that the action took effect, and the destination carries a heading (see 1). The residual gap is a missing focus move, which is a best practice, not the SC the finding cites — 2.4.3 Focus Order governs the order focusable components receive focus, and is not violated by a same-focus content swap. 4.1.3 Status Messages governs messages announced without focus change; a whole-region view swap the user initiated is not a status message. 3. Sub-claim 2 refutes itself. It says the dynamically inserted `role="alert"` at App.svelte:404 "works in most engines" and offers no failure it observed. Dynamic `role="alert"` insertion is reliably announced in current browser/AT pairs, and the codebase uses this same pattern consistently in four places (App.svelte:356, :404, :458, Journey.svelte:219). A hedged generic concern with no reproduction is not a defect. 4. The plan's own U11 criteria are met exactly, not partially. `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-dubplate-uploader.md:819-822` scopes the region to "announcements at >=25% progress deltas and on state changes only; completion is a distinct final announcement," where "state" is the journey state. The implementation exceeds that by also announcing transfer progress from App level (App.svelte:190-200). 5. The proposed fix for sub-claim 3 would regress accessibility. Stripping `role="alert"`/`role="status"` from OutcomeAlert (OutcomeAlert.svelte:33, 55, 64, 73) and Journey.svelte:190/219 leaves only the live region's one-line text — e.g. "No MusicBrainz match for this album." — announced, while the actionable body (the Private Recordings offer, the fix-names guidance, the three buttons) becomes silent until the user navigates to it. That trades a redundancy for an information loss. What genuinely survives, at minor severity: the double-announce is real. On `pushed-back`, Journey.svelte:152 writes the polite region and OutcomeAlert.svelte:33 injects an assertive `role="alert"` carrying overlapping content; same shape for probe-unavailable (155 / :55), stalled (177 / :73), queued (179 / :64), format-rejected (158 / Journey.svelte:219), and in-library (announceCompletion at 175 / `role="status"` at Journey.svelte:190). That is verbosity worth trimming — but by dropping the redundant one-line `announceState` calls in Journey, not by removing the alert roles. Also minor: the two `-> uploading` transitions (App.svelte:144, :279) land on headingless content, so a heading or a short `announceState` there would help. Neither rises to "would embarrass in front of family" or "breaks a contract."

refuted.title: Journey step status is conveyed by color and a CSS-generated glyph only
refuted.detail:
`JourneySteps.svelte:71-79` communicates each step's state through `colorClass()` (`step-success` / `step-primary` / `step-error` / none) plus `data-content`, which DaisyUI renders as `.steps .step[data-content]:after{content:attr(data-content)}` — CSS generated content on a pseudo-element. `aria-current="step"` marks only the current step. Nothing exposes "complete", "error", or "upcoming" to assistive technology: generated content is inconsistently surfaced across engine/AT pairs, and "✓" / "!" are not meaningful names even when it is.

So for a screen-reader user, the pushed-back spine reads "Uploaded, all 4 tracks received / Checked, every file is CD-quality FLAC / Matching, checking MusicBrainz just a moment / In your library, ready to play" — the exact same text as a healthy in-progress upload, with no indication that step 2 or 3 has failed. WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, and 1.3.1 for the state that exists visually but not programmatically.

(In the current build the color half is dead too — see the semantic-token blocker — so today there is no signal at all, visual or programmatic, beyond a bare unringed "!".)
refuted.fix:
Add a visually-hidden status word inside each `
  • `, driven off the same `statuses` array: `{status === 'complete' ? 'completed' : status === 'error' ? 'failed' : status === 'current' ? 'in progress' : 'not started'}`. That fixes 1.4.1 and 1.3.1 together and costs nothing visually.
refuted.verifier_reasoning: Mechanically the finding is right that JourneySteps.svelte:71-79 exposes step state only via colorClass() and data-content, with aria-current on the current step alone. But the stated harm is refuted by the same view. Journey.svelte:86-102 emits an `error` status only in the pushed-back, probe-unavailable, format-rejected, and stalled branches, and Journey.svelte:210-223 renders an OutcomeAlert (role="alert", headings "No MusicBrainz match" / "Can't check MusicBrainz right now") or the inline role="alert" "Couldn't add this album" block as a sibling directly below the spine for every one of those. Journey.svelte:146-163 additionally fires announceForViewMode() into the shared live region, which is genuinely wired: App.svelte:81/91/332 constructs the LiveRegion, attaches it to the unconditional <div aria-live="polite" role="status" class="sr-only">, and passes it at App.svelte:443-447. So the claim that a screen-reader user hears "the exact same text as a healthy in-progress upload, with no indication that step 2 or 3 has failed" is false; the failure is announced by both the alert role and the polite region. The WCAG 1.4.1 half is also refuted: state is not color-only, since complete renders "✓" and error renders "!" via data-content, visible in rejected-journey-desktop-1440.jpg (step 1 "✓", step 2 "!", steps 3/4 numbers) even with the semantic tokens dead — the finding itself concedes the glyph exists. What actually remains is that a screen-reader user cannot tell which step the failure attaches to, and cannot distinguish complete from upcoming beyond the position implied by aria-current="step" (the ARIA-sanctioned marker for this pattern). With the adjacent alert stating the failure in contract copy, that residual is minor polish, not a major pre-ship defect. The proposed sr-only fix is cheap and worth doing, but the finding as filed overstates both the impact and the WCAG basis.

refuted.title: Production serve never wires TagProbe: no main-lane upload can ever reach the library, and every one leaks its staged directory forever
refuted.detail:
`Options.TagProbe` is documented as "production wiring of the real probe is cmd/dubplate/serve.go's job" (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/upload.go:176-179). It is not wired. `NewServer` builds the Engine with `Options{Now, OnPromoted, TusBasePath}` only (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/internal/serve/serve.go:132-136), and `runServe` passes no probe either (/var/home/glw907/Projects/dubplate/cmd/dubplate/serve.go:43-47). `NewEngine` therefore installs `unavailableTagProbe`, which always returns `ErrTagProbeUnavailable` (upload.go:212-213, 123-125).

Concrete outcome for a family member on the deployed box: they upload a perfectly good FLAC album to the default collection, the format gate passes, `completeSession` takes the `err != nil` branch (upload.go:651-655), sets `ProbeUnavailable`, and returns. `promoteInto` is never called, so nothing is renamed into the inbox and the importer never sees it. The page shows the honest "retry later" state forever, because there is no retry: every subsequent attempt hits the same hardcoded failure. Only a session created against the exact `privateCollection` string bypasses the probe (upload.go:642-646) — and on the running dev instance that collection is not even in the configured collection list, so that escape hatch is closed too (see the separate private-lane finding).

Second-order damage: a `ProbeUnavailable` session is marked `completed` and its staged directory is deliberately left under UploadsDir ("leaves the session staged and unpromoted rather than discarding it", upload.go:620-624). `Store.expired` only returns sessions where `!completed` (session.go:330-334), so the sweep will never reclaim it and nothing else on the box does. Every main-lane upload permanently consumes disk until `archive.FreeSpace` drops under `FreeFloorGB` (5 GiB default) and `preCreate` starts rejecting everything with `ReasonNoSpace`.
refuted.fix: Wire the real U8 beets-matcher PROBE into `NewServerDeps`/`Options.TagProbe` before this ships, and make `NewServer` refuse to start when it is nil rather than silently falling back to `unavailableTagProbe` — a fail-closed default is right for a unit test, wrong for a composition root. Separately, give `ProbeUnavailable` and `PushedBack` sessions a real reclamation path (see the sweep findings).
